title: Client adaptive windowing & semantic-boundary-preserving SSE reconnect
creator: Aisha Verma
description:
Background: Several customer reports and internal QA runs exposed two recurring failure modes in long-lived server-sent event (SSE) streams: 1) clients rejoined after transient network loss and received partial JSON/tool-call fragments leading to duplicate or malformed function calls; 2) naive reconnects replayed byte-offset based fragments which caused ordering glitches when server-side batching or chunk coalescing changed during rollout. Both cases manifest most for structured outputs (JSONL or length-prefixed function calls) and for tool/function-calling flows where atomicity matters.

Goals:
- Provide a robust client-side reconnect strategy that minimizes duplicate/malformed structured outputs while preserving low tail-latency for interactive flows.
- Make reconnect semantics model/version-aware so servers can safely evolve chunking/batching without breaking clients.
- Preserve tool/function-call atomicity: no client-observed partial function calls, and safe deduplication when the same function-call is replayed after reconnect.
- Surface clear observability and fallbacks so rollouts can be monitored and reverted with low blast radius.

Non-goals:
- Replacing server-side resume tokens entirely; server resume tokens remain the authoritative mechanism when available.
- Heavy-weight protocol changes for all customers; this is a compatibility-layer-first approach with opt-in via SDK defaults and headers.

Proposal (high level):
1) Client adaptive windowing: clients maintain a small sliding "resume safe window" measured in semantic boundaries (see #2) rather than raw bytes. On reconnect, clients will attempt resume using the server-provided resume token if available; if not, they will claim the last fully-observed semantic boundary and request the server to resume after that boundary via a newly defined header X-Redwood-Resume-After: <boundary-id>.

2) Semantic boundaries and provenance markers: servers will annotate emitted chunks with lightweight provenance metadata embedded in the SSE comment/event envelope: boundary-id (monotonic per-session), boundary-type (json-line, functioncall, plain-text), and checksum of the chunk payload. For compatibility, these markers are optional and ignored by older clients; newer clients use them to know whether the last observed boundary was complete.

3) Token-aware flush hints: the runtime will inject flush hints where it can guarantee that a functioncall or JSON object is complete. Flush hints are represented as a comment event with boundary-type=functioncall and boundary-id. The SDK will only consider a functioncall "durable" after observing its flush hint.

4) Reconnect heuristics and backoff negotiation: clients will perform a three-step reconnect negotiation: (a) probe endpoint /v1/stream/health?resume=1 to check resume-token validity; (b) if resume token valid, reuse; (c) otherwise advertise last observed boundary-id using X-Redwood-Resume-After and allow server to choose safe replay point. Backoff uses server-suggested Retry-After and exponential jitter.

5) Dedup keys and idempotency: for function calls, the server will assign (and emit) an idempotency key per function-call boundary. Clients will preserve the most-recent idempotency keys and submit them on reconnect to enable server-side dedup.

6) SDK defaults & opt-in header: new clients (SDK >= 2.7) enable semantic-boundary resume by default; hosted endpoints will accept both old and new modes. The client will send X-Redwood-Resume-Mode: semantic|byte on connect to declare preference.

Implementation notes (server/runtime):
- Add an optional boundary metadata envelope to the SSE formatter path. Envelope is textual comments preceding events to be SSE-compatible. Implement kernel-level stamps where chunk coalescing happens so boundary-id remains stable even if batching size changes.
- When emitting function-call boundaries, runtime must flush the KV cache prefix for that request to avoid later KVC collisions on replayed prefixes.
- Resume token compatibility: token validators must accept resume-after boundary-id and map to an internal epoch; if mapping fails, server falls back to safe epoch earlier and include X-Redwood-Resume-Granted: <boundary-id> header to indicate where replay will start.

Implementation notes (clients/SDK):
- Track last-observed complete-boundary metadata per session: {boundary-id, checksum, idempotency-keys[], sequence}. Persist this to on-disk session store for long-lived apps (e.g., mobile background).
- On reconnect: prefer resume-token flow; if not present, use Resume-After flow and accept server-granted boundary. If the server indicates a mismatch in checksum, SDK should request a small rewind window (server may suggest boundary N-2) to reconcile partial writes.

Compatibility and rollout:
- The server will emit boundary comments only when the Accept header includes application/vnd.redwood.sse+json or when client advertises X-Redwood-Resume-Mode: semantic. This prevents older clients from seeing unfamiliar comments unless opted-in.
- Start rollout behind runtime flag in canary region, enable SDK opt-in for experiment, gather metrics for 4 weeks, then flip default in SDK and server-side accept header.

Trade-offs considered:
- Byte-offset resume is simple but fragile when batching changes; semantic boundaries add complexity but provide resiliency across churn.
- Full end-to-end message signing (HMAC on every chunk) would be more robust but adds latency and cost — chosen to keep low overhead while still giving checksum hints.

Edge cases:
- Interleaved functioncalls across multiplexed streams: boundary-ids are session-scoped; multiplexing uses lane-id + boundary-id to keep atomicity.
- Partial tool outputs that are long-running: for long tool outputs we will emit periodic heartbeat boundary comments to allow safe partial replay windows and avoid repeating entire long outputs on reconnect.

Documentation and API surface changes:
- API: new optional headers: X-Redwood-Resume-Mode, X-Redwood-Resume-After, X-Redwood-Resume-Granted. New content-type application/vnd.redwood.sse+json for opt-in metadata.
- SDK: new SessionStore interface for persisting boundary metadata and a higher-level StreamResumeManager.

Acceptance criteria:
- "No observed client-visible partial functioncall" in our end-to-end probe harness across 1000 simulated reconnects (95th percentile)
- Resume latency for reconnects with semantic mode within 120ms median for short-lived sessions (< 30s)
- Dashboards show <0.1% increase in error-rate for existing SSE customers during canary rollout
- SDK automated tests covering checksum mismatch and server-granted rewind scenarios

Rollout plan:
acceptance_criteria: E2E probes: 1000 simulated transient disconnects with semantic resume show zero partial/malformed functioncall artifacts
Resume negotiation completes within target latency (median < 120ms for short sessions)
Canary telemetry shows no >0.1% regression in client-observed SSE errors
SDK tests and integration tests added and green in CI
Runtime flag gating in canary region, then staged global rollout over 2 weeks
rollout_plan: Implement server boundary envelope behind runtime flag (runtime-flag:semantic-boundaries)
SDK PR exposing SessionStore and StreamResumeManager and opt-in header
Deploy server canary in us-west1 with appleton customers only
Enable SDK opt-in via field experiment for mobile/web beta customers
Collect telemetry 2 weeks, iterate on boundary-id churn tolerance
Flip SDK default and enable server-wide accept header support
Monitor and validate for 2 more weeks then deprecate legacy resume-only docs
testing: Unit: SSE formatter emits boundary comments when Accept header set
Integration: client+server harness simulating packet loss and validating no duplicated functioncalls
Chaos: introduce server-side batching changes during live reconnect tests
Performance: measure additional CPU/latency overhead for boundary metadata emission
Regression: ensure legacy clients unaffected when headers not present
